betterCitation: Francis Bacon, The Essays or Counsels, Civil and Moral, Of Studies (1625, modernised spelling)
reason: Refuted on the locator and on what the source line claims about the edition. The wording itself holds and I confirmed it against the named text rather than trusting the report: I downloaded Project Gutenberg ebook 575 and read Of Studies in full at lines 4306 to 4348. The sentence is there character for character, Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse; but to weigh and consider. So there is no drift and no splice, and the quotation is a complete sentence ending in a full stop. FIRST FAULT, THE LOCATOR. The evidence calls it the sixth sentence of the essay. It is the seventh. Counting from the text as printed: (1) STUDIES serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability. (2) Their chief use for delight, is in privateness and retiring; for ornament, is in discourse; and for ability, is in the judgment, and disposition of business. (3) For expert men can execute, and perhaps judge of particulars, one by one; but the general counsels, and the plots and marshalling of affairs, come best, from those that are learned. (4) To spend too much time in studies is sloth; to use them too much for ornament, is affectation; to make judgment wholly by their rules, is the humor of a scholar. (5) They perfect nature, and are perfected by experience: for natural abilities are like natural plants, that need proyning, by study; and studies themselves, do give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded in by experience. (6) Crafty men contemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by observation. (7) Read not to contradict and confute. Off by one, and checkable, so the evidence record should not ship saying sixth. SECOND FAULT, THE EDITION. The source line names (1625), which on this track reads as the edition whose wording is being shipped, and the 1625 quarto is printed in original spelling. The wording that was actually matched is a modernised-spelling text, as the evidence itself concedes, and PG 575 declares no base edition at all, so strictly the wording is attested in an unidentified modern reprint. 1625 is the right edition for the CONTENT, since the short 1597 Of Studies reads only Reade not to contradict, nor to beleeue, but to waigh and consider, and the three-limbed sentence is the 1625 expansion. But the card as it stands claims 1625 wording it does not have. The track has already ruled this way twice: 03-fict-08 had to carry a note that putrifies is the 1883 edition's spelling, and 03-phil-04 had to say the wording is Hazlitt's revision of Cotton and not Cotton's own. The same note is owed here, and the note field is empty. Everything else is clean and I could not break it: attribution is Bacon's own prose in his own essay, no speaker owed, the misattribution list has no Bacon trap and the Francis Bacon on the Calendar For Life list, cflId 349, is the twentieth-century painter and a different man; shipped.js returns no hit, no near-hit, zero for the year, not banned, not at cap; Essay is the form of the work and the essay is titled Of Studies in a book called The Essays or Counsels, Civil and Moral, which is as square as the tag gets; scope is clean, 1625, no scripture, no oratory, nothing needing a warning; the fame test passes, since this is the sentence the essay is known by alongside Reading maketh a full man; the theme is Wisdom and Counsel and the sentence is counsel in the imperative; the source line leads with the name, carries no dash and runs 73 characters. This should come back as CORRECTED, not VERIFIED.
